 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Kenrich Williams, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Williams, who played 26 minutes off the bench in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers, returns to the starting lineup. As a result, Alex Caruso will come off the bench after making a spot start in Portland. The other four starters are unchanged.

 OKC 
 Guard

 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Mitchell will miss a second straight game with an ankle injury. Alex Caruso started Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers and should hold onto that role. He is worth streaming with Mitchell out. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) is questionable to play against the Clippers on Friday. 
 Mitchell missed Wednesday’s game against Portland, which allowed Alex Caruso to slide into the starting unit. Caruso contributed 14 points, three steals and four triples in the loss and would be worth streaming if Mitchell ends up missing another game. 
 Aday Mara 
 OKC 
 Center 
 #15 
 Aday Mara notched 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one block in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 For the first time in his young NBA career, Mara played over 30 minutes in a game. He logged 32 minutes against the Trail Blazers, but the final stat line wasn’t strong enough to make the rookie a must-start in all leagues. Mara replaced Kenrich Williams (11/2/2 with one block and two three-pointers) in the starting lineup, and who starts moving forward may be dictated by the opposition’s rotation. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso accounted for 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, three steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder didn’t have Ajay Mitchell for Wednesday’s game, opening a spot in the starting lineup for Caruso. He took advantage of the opportunity, shooting 4-of-5 from beyond the arc. Caruso’s 14 points were a new season high for him, as he totaled 17 points in the first four games he played upon returning from an ankle injury. If Mitchell remains out for Friday’s game against the Clippers, Caruso would be worth rostering in 14-team leagues and some 12-team leagues. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Jared McCain, Alex Caruso, Aday Mara and Isaiah Hartenstein will start Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 The Thunder have made two changes to the lineup that started Tuesday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. With Ajay Mitchell out, Caruso moves into the starting lineup. The other change is Mara, who replaces Kenrich Williams. 
 Ajay Mitchell 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #25 
 Ajay Mitchell (ankle) has been ruled out against the Trail Blazers on Wednesday. 
 Mitchell will be sidelined for the second night of OKC’s back-to-back, which will open up a spot in the starting unit. Alex Caruso, Micah Peavy and Nique Clifford are all candidates to take on more minutes, with one of them likely to start. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is not on the injury report for Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Caruso is back after missing Oklahoma City’s last three games with a sprained ankle. He’ll give the Thunder much-needed wing depth, with two-way contract rookie Josh Dix possibly falling out of the rotation. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is not expected to be out long term 
 After missing this third straight contest on Monday vs. the Cavs, Caruso is expected to not be out long term as his ankle sprain is not deemed serious. Even when the veteran guard gets back into the fold, the Thunder will still rely on the younger guys for heavy minutes. 
 Alex Caruso 
 OKC 
 Guard 
 #9 
 Alex Caruso (ankle) is out for Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Monday’s game will be the third that Caruso has missed since spraining his right ankle during Oklahoma City’s October 26 win over the Suns. Injuries have forced the Thunder to go deep into their bench, with rookie Bennett Stirtz playing 25 minutes or more in each of the last three games. 
 Kenrich Williams 
 OKC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #34 
 Kenrich Williams finished Saturday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists and three three-pointers. 
 After totaling 10 points in his first two starts of the season, Williams scored 11 on Saturday. He was most valuable against the Rockets in three-pointers and rebounds, but this performance doesn’t make “Kenny Hustle” a must-add heading into Oklahoma City’s four-game Week 3. Also, with the Thunder playing two games against Cleveland to start the week, it’s fair to wonder whether head coach Mark Daigneault would consider a bigger lineup to match up with Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. If so, Williams or Jared McCain (10/4/2/1) could be headed to the bench.

 Brook Lopez accumulated 26 points (11-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Thunder.
 After coming off the bench in the Clippers’ first six games, Lopez is approaching the point where he needs to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He’s scored at least 20 points in three of the last four games, with Friday’s total being a season high. Add in the rebounds and three-pointers, and this was a good night for those rostering the veteran center. Isaiah Jackson (5/3/3 with one block), who began the season as the starter, should be rostered only in very deep leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Darius Garland 
 LAC 
 Guard

 Player Stats

 Darius Garland finished Friday’s win over the Thunder with 24 points (8-of-17 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, seven assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 After being outscored 40-25 in the third quarter, Garland and the Clippers did what needed to be done down the stretch to win the 113-112 thriller. The Clippers’ starting point guard had the game’s biggest shot: a layup through contact and an ensuing free throw with 50.4 seconds left to take the lead for good. Even with the occasional struggles with turnovers, Garland is providing top-100 fantasy value through 11 games. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Domantas Sabonis put up 21 points (9-of-16 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 12 rebounds, five assists, and a three in the loss on Friday to the Blazers. 
 After a really bad game against the Magic, Sabonis bounced back and went back to his usual self against the Blazers. He looked healthier in this game, which is a good sign. The efficiency has still been good, but it is starting to come down from his super-hot start. He still puts up good counting stats which is why you have Sabonis in the first place. Overall, its been a good season so far.
